# `pi_set_time`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Set the host time zone and calendar time, then update the mount's clock; the reply does not confirm any of it.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (64-bit and 32-bit builds) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, guider handler @0x72650 (64-bit guider build; no event-sender call), main-imager relay path; host-command behaviour from static analysis of the packaged scripts (both builds) |

Registered in the guider; the main imager relays the unknown method to the guider (command traffic arrives on the control port, the relay forwards the original request text). Params are an object or a one-element array holding it. If time_zone is nonempty a timezone script runs first; if all six calendar members differ from -1 the host date is then set. Both host attempts happen before the mount connection and capability are checked and are not rolled back. Only the timezone script's stdout is scanned for a lowercase 'error'; the date command's output is not parsed and child exit statuses are ignored, so a reply of code 0 does not prove the zone or calendar changed. An empty object attempts only the mount update. Last, the mount time is updated unless a view function is working (then that step is skipped and success is returned). No event is sent for a time or zone change; use pi_get_time to read the result back. No running process refreshes its zone after the change, so local-time fields may stay in the previous zone until the services restart (INFERRED). ViewPlan deadlines already computed keep their old values.

Side effects: Runs a host timezone script and a privileged date-set command, then writes the mount clock through the driver. No rollback. Shell commands are built with fixed size-bounded buffers; the zone name is not quoted.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"pi_set_time"`. [READ] |
| `params` | any | no | - | Either a direct object or an array whose first element is the object; one array level is unwrapped and later elements are ignored. The Android and iOS apps send the one-element array form (OBSERVED shape, 2026-10-12). [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (both) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (both) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | (success) The request method, echoed. [READ] |
| `result` | integer | yes | - | (success) For these methods the result is the integer 0. Fixed value `0`. [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (success) Fixed value `0`. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (success) Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |
| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (error) Nonzero. A requested code of 0 is coerced to 207. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (error) The request id echoed with its JSON type; null on dispatcher errors 100 and 200, where it is the only way to recognise the reply and cannot be matched to a request. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 107 | Params null or not an object after unwrapping one array level | `expected object param` |
| 214 | Output stream of a host command could not be read (thread-local error propagated) | `fail to run command` |
| 216 | The timezone script's stdout contains the lowercase text 'error'; the date and mount stages are skipped | `fail to set timezone` |
| 315 | Mount not connected after the host attempts | `mount is not connected` |
| 210 | No time capability on the mount | `not supported` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request is not an object, is an empty object, or has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: no method of type string (a non-string method counts as missing) | `invalid request` |
| 101 | Dispatcher: text fails to parse | `invalid JSON request: <reason> on line <n> ...` |
| 103 | Dispatcher: unregistered method | `method not found` |

Driver-originated codes from the mount update are unresolved.

## Example

Request, array-form - One-element array form sent by the apps (shape OBSERVED 2026-10-12; values invented):

```json
{"id":81,"method":"pi_set_time","params":[{"year":2026,"mon":10,"day":14,"hour":21,"min":5,"sec":30,"time_zone":"America/Chicago"}]}
```

Request, object-form - Direct object also accepted:

```json
{"id":82,"method":"pi_set_time","params":{"time_zone":"Etc/UTC"}}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"pi_set_time","result":0,"code":0,"id":81}
```

Reply, bad-params:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"pi_set_time","error":"expected object param","code":107,"id":83}
```
